ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a DC power supply labeled 12 V, with positive at the top and negative at the bottom; the positive terminal of the power supply is connected through the 1 kΩ resistor at the top to the output node on the right. This output node is simultaneously connected downward through the Zener diode Dz to the bottom reference rail, and connected to the right-side 2 kΩ load resistor to the bottom reference rail. The output voltage Uo is marked across the right-side 2 kΩ load, with the upper end positive and the lower end negative, so Dz and the 2 kΩ load share the same output voltage. Reasoning: The problem gives the breakdown voltage of Dz as 6 V. Treating Dz as an ideal Zener diode, if it enters the breakdown voltage-regulating state, the output node is clamped at 6 V. Current check: the current through the 1 kΩ series resistor is (12 V - 6 V) / 1 kΩ = 6 mA; the 2 kΩ load current is 6 V / 2 kΩ = 3 mA; the remaining 3 mA flows through Dz, and the Zener diode current is positive, indicating that the breakdown voltage-regulating condition is satisfied. Therefore, the output voltage Uo = 6 V.

raw_record.question_text: In the voltage regulator circuit shown in the figure, given that the breakdown voltage of the diode \(D_z\) is 6 V, the output voltage \(U_o\) = ________ V.

method.method_draft: First describe the circuit: the 12 V supply goes through a 1 kΩ resistor to the output node; Dz and the 2 kΩ load are both connected between this node and the bottom reference rail, so they share the same voltage as Uo. From the text, the zener breakdown voltage is 6 V. Treat Dz as an ideal zener regulator and set the node voltage to 6 V, then check that current can sustain breakdown: the series resistor supplies 6 mA and the load draws 3 mA, leaving 3 mA through Dz. Since the zener current is positive, the clamp condition is consistent, so Uo = 6 V.
